title: MCP 2026-07-28: The Stateless Spec Update
content:
## Overview

On July 28, 2026, the Model Context Protocol maintainers finalized the **2026-07-28 revision** — the most substantial change to the spec since authorization was added. It re-architects MCP's core around statelessness, and includes changes that are **not backward compatible** with older clients and servers.

---

## Why It Changed

MCP was originally designed for servers running on a developer's own machine, talking to a local client over stdio. As MCP servers moved into the cloud — run by companies behind APIs, serving many concurrent clients — the original stateful session model became a scalability bottleneck. A stateful server has to pin each client to the specific process instance holding its session, which fights standard cloud infrastructure like load balancers and autoscaling groups.

---

## What Changed

**Stateless core.** The base protocol no longer requires a server to hold per-client session state between requests. This lets MCP servers run behind ordinary load balancers on standard Kubernetes/DevOps tooling, the same way REST APIs do — requests become cacheable and routable rather than sticky to one server instance.

**Stronger authorization.** The revision brings tighter OAuth 2.1 and OIDC-based authorization flows, aimed at closing gaps that had emerged as MCP servers started handling enterprise credentials and multi-tenant access.

**Tasks moved out of core.** The Tasks feature (used for tracking long-running operations) is no longer part of the base spec — it's now a **versioned extension**, so implementations that don't need long-running task tracking aren't forced to support it. Anthropic has committed to keeping deprecated core features functional for at least 12 months after deprecation.

**New connector capabilities.** The update also standardizes several features enterprise MCP deployments had been building ad hoc: embedded UI (servers can return renderable UI fragments, not just data), enterprise-managed authentication, built-in observability hooks, and private network tunnels for connecting to internal-only services without exposing them publicly.

---

## Compatibility

This is explicitly a breaking change. A client built against an older revision may not interoperate with a 2026-07-28 server, and vice versa — implementations need to negotiate protocol version explicitly. Anthropic and the MCP maintainers are treating this as a deliberate one-time architectural correction rather than the start of a faster-moving breaking-change cadence.

---

## Why It Matters for Claude Code

Claude Code is one of the most common MCP clients in the wild (see [Tool Use & Agents](tool-use-and-agents)), and this session's own tool list is built from MCP servers (GitHub, Slack, Google Drive, and more). The stateless core means MCP server operators can scale connectors the same way they scale any other web backend, and the new enterprise-auth and private-tunnel features are aimed squarely at the pattern of "connect Claude Code to internal company systems" that had previously required bespoke, non-standard workarounds.

---

## Key Dates

| Date | Event |
|---|---|
| Nov 2024 | MCP first released by Anthropic |
| — | Authorization (OAuth) added to the spec |
| July 28, 2026 | 2026-07-28 revision: stateless core, Tasks extracted to extension, enterprise connector features |
